mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, lower real interest rates incentivize equity investment, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean of returns during similar low-rate periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) followed by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month signals a labor market softening that reduces equity risk aversion and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 and UNRATE < prev UNRATE within the same month
regime_hint: Transition from tight labor market to moderation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under this signal are not statistically outperforming the 30-day rolling mean across 5 such regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests strengthening economic momentum, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 2% MoM in current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such acceleration events are not statistically positive vs. prior 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two consecutive months reduces expectations of rate hikes, lowering discount rates and supporting positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during sustained CPIAUCSL < 3% periods are not higher than the 30-day rolling mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly housing starts index (HOUST) rises by more than 10% in a month, it indicates resilient housing demand and a supportive macro backdrop that increases the probability of positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns under this signal are not significantly higher than the 5-day moving average during 10 such events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) followed by a sustained rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) indicates a recovery in labor supply, which reduces risk premia and tends to produce negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < prev UNRATE by > 0.2pp and PAYEMS > prev PAYEMS for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such labor recovery signals are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (not available in provided proxies; fallback to RSAFS as proxy for demand) below -2% for 3 months indicates weakening demand, which typically precedes equity drawdowns and predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such contraction are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) move in opposite directions (INDPRO up > 2% while CPIAUCSL down > 0.5%), it creates a supply-side divergence that increases uncertainty and is associated with negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 2% and CPIAUCSL < prev CPIAUCSL by > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such divergent signals are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean across 4 such events (p > 0.05).
